reading.title: The Cables Beneath the Sea
reading.intro_zh: Lesson 4 讲的是“远方的人生更新”，而这篇拓展阅读把镜头转向真实世界：让这些跨洋消息得以传递的海底通信电缆。文章改编自学术媒体 The Conversation 上昆尼皮亚克大学网络安全学者 Robin Chataut 的署名科普文章。

source.title: Undersea cables are the unseen backbone of the global internet

passage: Whenever a message races from one continent to another, it almost certainly travels through a cable resting on the floor of the ocean. According to cybersecurity researcher Robin Chataut, more than ninety-five percent of the world's data crosses these submarine cables rather than passing through satellites overhead. Although each cable is typically no wider than a garden hose, it contains slender strands of glass that carry information as pulses of light. Roughly 485 such cables, stretching for more than 900,000 miles in total, now lace the seabed, quietly linking distant cities that most people will never visit.

Sending a signal across an entire ocean is far from effortless. Because light gradually weakens as it travels, devices called repeaters are spaced along each cable to amplify the fading pulses and keep the data intact. Laying a single cable is an enormous undertaking that can stretch over months or even years, depending on the route. Once installed, the cables remain surprisingly vulnerable: an estimated 100 to 150 are damaged each year, usually when fishing equipment or a ship's anchor accidentally drags across the seabed. Specialised vessels must then locate the break, haul the cable to the surface, and splice it back together.

What makes this hidden network remarkable is how invisible it remains. A student video-calling a cousin abroad, or downloading a photograph sent from a faraway harbour, rarely imagines the journey those signals undertake beneath thousands of metres of water. Yet without this submerged infrastructure, the sense that the world has grown smaller would quickly disappear, and a familiar face on a distant continent would feel genuinely out of reach.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Satellites have replaced cables as the chief carrier of global data.
Undersea cables are dangerous and should be removed from the ocean.
A vast, largely invisible network of undersea cables carries most of the world's data and keeps continents connected.
Sending a single message across the ocean is now cheap and instant for everyone.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文围绕海底电缆这一“看不见的网络”展开：它承载了全球绝大部分数据、把各大洲连在一起，这是文章的主旨。其余选项要么与原文相反（卫星取代电缆、电缆应被移除），要么是细枝末节，并非中心思想。

questions.question: According to the passage, how much of the world's data travels through submarine cables?
options: More than ninety-five percent.
Roughly half.
About 485 percent.
Less than ten percent.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中明确写道 more than ninety-five percent of the world's data crosses these submarine cables。485 是电缆的数量，不是百分比，属于干扰项。

questions.question: When a submarine cable is accidentally cut by an anchor, what happens next according to the passage?
options: The cable is left on the seabed and a satellite takes over permanently.
Repeaters automatically grow a new section of glass fibre.
The damage is ignored because cables almost never break.
Specialised vessels find the break, lift the cable to the surface, and splice it back together.
questions.explanation_zh: 原文说当电缆被损坏后，Specialised vessels must then locate the break, haul the cable to the surface, and splice it back together，描述的正是修复流程。其它选项均无文中依据。

questions.question: What can be inferred about repeaters from the passage?
options: They are only needed on cables shorter than a garden hose.
Without them, a light signal would fade too much to cross an entire ocean.
They are the main reason cables are cut by fishing equipment.
They make satellites unnecessary for any kind of communication.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中说 light gradually weakens as it travels，而 repeaters 的作用是 amplify the fading pulses and keep the data intact。由此可推断：没有中继器，光信号会衰减到无法跨越整个大洋。这是基于因果关系的合理推断。

questions.question: In the final paragraph, the cables are called a 'submerged infrastructure.' The word 'submerged' most nearly means:
options: extremely expensive
recently invented
underwater
easy to see
questions.explanation_zh: 整篇文章都在讲电缆铺设在海底（on the floor of the ocean、beneath thousands of metres of water），因此 submerged 在此语境中意为“被水淹没的、水下的”，即 underwater。

writing.intro_zh: 今天的仿写仍抓住 Lesson 4 的五个“远方人生更新”句型，但把语境升级到更抽象、更成熟的层面：刚收到的消息、在某地停留了多久、到目前为止已经去过哪些地方、已经动身前往某地，以及第一次走出国门带来的全新体验。

patterns.title: have just received ... from ...
patterns.source: I have just received a letter from my brother, Tim.
patterns.focus_zh: 用 have just received...from... 写一条刚到的消息、邮件、照片或电话更新。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：用 have just received...from... 描述你刚收到的一条带来重要消息或转折的更新，并说明它让你产生了什么想法或感受。
patterns.sample: I have just received a detailed voice message from my cousin in Canada, and it suddenly made my quiet hometown feel connected to a far larger world.
patterns.tip_zh: have just received 强调“刚收到”；from 后面写消息来自谁，再用一个分句说明这条消息带来的影响。

patterns.title: has been there for ...
patterns.source: He has been there for six months.
patterns.focus_zh: has been there for... 表示某人从过去到现在一直在那个地方。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：某人在国外或外地长期生活或工作，已经在那里待了一段时间，并补充一个细节说明这段时间带来的变化。
patterns.sample: My cousin now works for an engineering firm in Vancouver, and she has been there for almost a year, slowly turning a strange city into a second home.
patterns.tip_zh: there 指前面已经提到的地点；for 后面接一段时间，再用一个分句体现这段时间累积出的变化。

patterns.title: has already visited ...
patterns.source: He has already visited a great number of different places.
patterns.focus_zh: has already visited... 把“到现在为止已经完成的旅行经历”说出来。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：某人到目前为止已经去过若干个不同的地方，并说明这些经历对他/她产生了怎样的影响。
patterns.sample: In just a few months abroad, she has already visited several remote towns and coastal harbours that completely changed how she pictures the rest of the world.
patterns.tip_zh: already 放在 has 后面，visited 后面接去过的地方，再补充这些地方带来的认知改变。

patterns.title: has gone to ...
patterns.source: He has gone to Alice Springs.
patterns.focus_zh: has gone to... 表示某人已经去了某地，现在不在原来的地方或还没回来。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：某人已经动身前往一个较远的地方，目前不在原处，并说明他/她接下来打算做什么。
patterns.sample: My elder brother has gone to a research station in the mountains, and he will not return until the long winter survey is finally complete.
patterns.tip_zh: 不要把 has gone to 和 has been to 混在一起；这里强调人已经出发去了那里、暂时不在原处，并交代后续安排。

patterns.title: has never been abroad before
patterns.source: My brother has never been abroad before.
patterns.focus_zh: has never been abroad before 表示过去到现在都没有过出国经历，所以这次是第一次。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：某人此前从未出过国，因此这次的学习、工作或旅行带来一种既兴奋又紧张的全新体验。
patterns.sample: My sister has never been abroad before, so every unfamiliar street sign and crowded station fills her with a mixture of excitement and nervous wonder.
patterns.tip_zh: before 放在句末很自然；后半句可以用更具体的细节解释这种第一次出国时的复杂心情。
